blocks.text: Witness statement of DEBORAH MOORE (read)
This is a statement from Deborah Moore dated 21 February 2018. In it, she says:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I am a band 6 midwife. I qualified as a midwife in October of 2004. In April 2010 I began working at the Countess of Chester Hospital and I've worked on the antenatal ward, post-natal ward, labour ward, community midwifery and antenatal clinic.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: I currently work in the delivery suite at the Countess of Chester Hospital. My role within the delivery suite is to triage
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: and assess pregnant women who attend the hospital, I will give advice to those who do not require admitting to the labour ward, and those who require admittance will be allocated a midwife who will monitor and support women during labour and look after mother and baby postnatally.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "My core role is to provide care to ensure maternal and foetal well-being. There are four different ways a baby can be delivered: they are normal birth, where the baby is born normally by a midwife; instrumental birth, where doctors are involved where forceps and ventouse are used; elective caesarean, where the parents elect to have the baby born by this method for a number of different reasons and this will have been agreed with a doctor prior to birth; and the fourth and final option, emergency caesarean. This is an emergency operation completed where there are complications with either the mother or baby and the baby needs to be delivered.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "As a midwife, if I am caring for a mother, I will be present during any of these procedures regardless of whether doctors or surgery is involved. Other than during my placements I have never worked on a neonatal unit and I have never worked on the neonatal unit at the Countess of Chester Hospital. During my normal duties if a baby is born requiring admittance to the neonatal unit, I will speak with staff on there to get updates on the baby's health and progress, which will then be passed on to the new parents.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I have been asked to comment on the birth of baby [Baby H] who was born on 22 September 2015.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Having reviewed the maternity notes, I can see that I attended at room 11 in the delivery suite at approximately 18.00 hours on this day to take [Baby H]'s mum, [Mother of Baby H], to theatre for an emergency caesarean procedure.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "[Mother of Baby H] was on a sliding scale due to her diabetes and the decision for an emergency caesarean was made as [Mother of Baby H] was struggling to manage her blood sugars which can have an effect on the placenta.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: A sliding scale is an insulin infusion, which is altered according to the mother's blood sugars.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "As a midwife I will ensure the mother is prepared for the caesarean procedure. The mother is then transferred to theatre, either by walking across or being transferred on a bed.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "A typical caesarean operation would involve an anaesthetist, assistant anaesthetist, surgeon, who was a registrar or
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: consultant, surgeon's assistant, scrub nurse, midwife and runner.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "If an emergency caesarean is required at least one paediatrician is also present. All of these people need to be present for a caesarean operation to take place so they will have been present for the birth of [Baby H].
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "[Baby H] was born at 18.22 hours and was in good condition, weighing 2,330 grams, which is acceptable for a baby born at 34 weeks.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "[Baby H]'s Apgar score was 7 at minute 1 and 10 at minute 5, which is good. The Apgar score is used to measure the physical condition of a newborn baby and includes skin colour, responsiveness, heart rate, respiratory efforts and muscle tone. Her cord gas readings were also normal. [Baby H]'s birth was an uneventful birth (she did not require any additional treatment or intervention).
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "The placenta was delivered normally without complications. [Baby H] was transferred to the neonatal unit due to her prematurity. I do not recall having any other involvement with [Mother of Baby H] or [Baby H]."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Witness statement of DR JONATHAN FORD (read)
Moving on, my Lord, please, to Jonathan Ford, who was a consultant. His statement dated is 21 September 2022:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I am a consultant obstetrician and gynaecologist currently working at the Leighton Hospital. I was present and assisted with the birth of [Baby H].
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "[Mother of Baby H] had diabetes, requiring insulin. She used an insulin pump for her diabetes.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: She was admitted to hospital at 34 plus 2 gestation.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: This was because her blood sugars were low and she was requiring less and less insulin. She had two doses of antenatal steroids administered for foetal lung maturity. Due to her declining insulin requirements and episodes of hypoglycaemia, she required a category 3 emergency caesarean section at 34 plus 4 gestation.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "The caesarean section was performed under a spinal anaesthetic and baby delivered on 22 September 2015."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: And we know, my Lord, despite what the statement says, that was at 18.22 hours. I'm sure I can do that with agreement. There's an error in the consultant's statement:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "The caesarean section was uneventful and there were no complications. Baby was born in good condition with Apgar scores of 7 at birth and 10 at 5 minutes. Her cord gases were arterial pH 7.34, BE 0.3, venous 7.39 and BE 0.6..."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think that's base excess as we heard, I think, earlier in the trial.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "... confirming good condition at birth. We perform elective caesarean sections at or after 39 weeks' gestation. Babies born by caesarean section before this gestation are more likely to have difficulty with their breathing (respiratory distress syndrome). They are more likely to struggle to maintain their
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: body temperature. Her gestation and the presence of maternal diabetes meant that she was at high risk of developing hypoglycaemia in the neonatal period. It was for these reasons that the paediatricians were present in theatre for the delivery and that she was admitted to the neonatal unit."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: That concludes his statement, my Lord.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Witness statement of DR KHALIL LUKE GEORGE VARGHESE (read)
The next statement I am going to read is that of a Dr Varghese. That's at 34 of my Lord's bundle, so in the new section today.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Dr Varghese's statement is dated 6 March 2018. His full name being, I should say, Khalil Luke George Varghese. He says as follows:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I have been asked to comment on the care and treatment of baby [Baby H] and in particular her care on 24 September 2015."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: My Lord, I should say the next three statements that we are going to read are not represented by medical notes in the sequence of events chart. They set the scene, really, for the two events which the Crown allege in this particular baby's case. So these are setting the scene for the shifts of the 25th into the 26th and the subsequent shift, the 26th into the 27th if that helps.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Right. You understand what Mr Astbury is saying? You don't have medical notes relating to what is being described in this witness's statement, but because it's agreed evidence -- obviously there are medical notes, they're just not in the sequence of events -- just listen carefully to it, but there aren't notes to which you can refer by way of documents as far as this is concerned.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: If anyone needs to return to them, they can be made available, but I don't think it's necessary.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: All right.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: "I have been asked to comment on the care and treatment of [Baby H] and in particular her care on 24 September 2015.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I was working a night shift, the 23rd into 24 September 2015. I can't recall what nursing staff were present upon my attendance or accurately recall what nursery [Baby H] was in.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Using the medical notes I can see that prior to my attendance, Dr Alison Ventress had documented that [Baby H] had been fine all night until 7 am. She had been on non-invasive ventilation, that being CPAP, but had then deteriorated, had poor gas, and was having profound desaturations with low oxygen levels.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Her heart rate was fine and she was placed on more support, that being BiPAP, that being an abbreviation for biphasic positive airway pressure, which gives additional respiratory support. A cold light test was conducted to check for any air leak, but this was shown as normal.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "[Baby H] looked mottled and her capillary refill time was approximately 3 seconds. [Baby H] was given a fluid bolus. Her breathing was poor with a gasping pattern.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: [Baby H]'s oxygen level requirement was now 60% and Dr Ventress made the decision to ventilate [Baby H].
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "As this was an elective intubation, having had experience of this procedure on previous placements with Dr Ventress, I asked if I could carry out the procedure.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I made an entry on the medical records of [Baby H] at 08.10 hours that day, stating that I had completed the intubation checklist, which included prescribing [Baby H] the medicines as per the policy."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: And then he specifies that that's the neonatal elective intubation checklist:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I inserted a size 3.5 endotracheal tube through the vocal cords and into her lungs. It was 8.5 centimetres at the lips, but when I listened in, there was reduced air entry on one side, so I pulled back the endotracheal tube to 8 centimetres and ordered a chest X-ray.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "A plan was made to give [Baby H] surfactant once the chest Xray confirmed the position of the endotracheal tube. Surfactant is a lung product which neonates who are born early will be deficient in and this may have been the reason why her breathing had deteriorated.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "At 09.00 hours I made a further entry in the medical notes of [Baby H] stating that although she was on a ventilator, she was desaturating despite being in 100% oxygen. There are a number of things to check to try and identify the cause of the desaturation, which include: is there an issue with the machine, is the tube placed correctly, or to monitor CO2 levels to check the tube is sited correctly. I conducted the carbon dioxide test with [Baby H], which showed that the tube was in the correct position.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I would have listened to her air entry, which was present on both sides, but was reduced on the left side which had previously been noted. [Baby H]'s sats showed 70% despite her being on 100% oxygen.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I did not feel comfortable dealing with such an unwell patient on my own so called for the registrar, who at this time was [Dr A]. [Dr A] attended to assist.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "He checked the endotracheal tube to ensure it was in the correct position, confirming it was through the cords. [Baby H] was given artificial breaths with a Neopuff with a longer inspiration time which appeared to have a good response from [Baby H], including increasing her tidal volumes, that being the volume of air displaced between a cycle of inspiration and expiration.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: On the ventilator as well..."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: I read that without the brackets, my Lord:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "It was a good response from [Baby H] including increasing her tidal volumes on the ventilator as well as [Baby H]'s improvement in clinical condition was sustained. We were able to reduce her oxygen requirements from 100% to 50%. A cold light test was completed, which showed transillumination on the left side, which is consistent with a pulmonary air leak or pneumothorax.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "As [Baby H] was now settled, it was decided to wait for a formal chest X-ray to review the pneumothorax and then decide on the most effective treatment. I had no further involvement with [Baby H]'s care that day."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: My Lord, that takes us to the morning of 24 September, the end of Dr Varghese's night shift.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Next, please, if we can read a statement from [Nurse B], which again is in the additional bundle that your Lordship received this morning. I'll just check the page number.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Witness statement of [NURSE B] (read)
Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: [Nurse B] signed her statement on 23 February 2018 and stated as follows:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Further to the statement I have already provided to Cheshire Police with reference to the investigation at the neonatal unit within the Countess of Chester Hospital, I would like to add the following.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I have been asked to comment on [Baby H]. Having reviewed the nursing and clinical notes, I can recall [Baby H]. She was born after 34 weeks and was a good weight. Her mum had diabetes, which sometimes can contribute towards the baby's extra weight. [Baby H] had a chest drain fitted, but I can recall there would regularly be yellow fluid within the chest drain tube which would normally indicate infection. [Baby H] was on antibiotics to try counteract any infection.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "On 24 September 2015, I started a long day shift at 7.30 am. At the start of my shift [Baby H] was in nursery 1 (ITU) and she'd been on CPAP but her work of breathing was significantly increased, indicating the CPAP was not enough for her and, as a result, she was due to be intubated with an endotracheal tube which would be attached to a ventilator. A ventilator breathes for you, whereas CPAP supports your breathing.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I took over designated nurse duties for [Baby H] from the night nurse, Lucy Letby. Due to the emergency intubation required for [Baby H] we had a very quick handover as we prepared [Baby H] for intubation.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Also present was Dr Alison Ventress and senior house officer George Varghese. [Baby H] was given intubation drugs and I recall her being quite active, which is a good sign. I believe that the intubation process was completed with no complications. Once [Baby H] was settled and stable, I will have had a handover with Lucy, who will have gone off duty as she was the night staff.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "[Baby H] had a chest X-ray immediately after intubation to ensure the endotracheal tube was in the correct place. A capnograph was fitted to the endotracheal tube and if the tube is fitted correctly in the lungs this will turn yellow. If the endotracheal tube had gone down the oesophagus and into the stomach it would turn (inaudible). The capnograph for [Baby H] showed yellow changes, which indicated it was fitted correctly.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I listened to [Baby H]'s chest using a stethoscope and could tell it was slightly quieter on the left side than the right. The doctor performing the intubation would pull the endotracheal tube back slightly, resulting in equal chest movement and air entry. At this point a chest X-ray would have been requested by the doctors.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "[Baby H] was on standard ventilation with not too high pressure or rates. She was on 50% oxygen and I recorded on my notes that she had never been in air prior to intubation.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "At 8.35 hours [Baby H]'s saturations dropped to 54% and she had quieter air entry on the left side but still had chest movement on both sides and the capnograph was still turning yellow. Senior House Officer Varghese was still on the ward at this time and increased the rate and pressures on [Baby H]'s ventilator, but there was still no improvement. He took over manually ventilating [Baby H] with a Neopuff in case there was a mechanical failure with the ventilator.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "We crash bleeped the duty registrar to attend and Registrar [Dr A] attended and increased the inspiratory time, which improved the oxygen saturations and [Baby H] was placed back on the ventilator.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "At 08.40 Registrar Dave Harkness was also present with [Baby H]. Registrar Harkness wanted to view the chest X-ray images on a computer screen to establish the most appropriate site for a chest drain. There was a delay in getting the X-rays on the computer screen and as a result I completed a Datix [that's a clinical incident] form.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I did not leave the nursery while looking after [Baby H]. Had I needed to leave at any point then I would have arranged cover and a baby who was on a ventilator would never be left unattended.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "At 10.05 hours [Baby H] had an acute desaturation on the ventilator and was not responding to the Neopuff.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Registrar Dave Harkness inserted an emergency chest drain after a positive cold light.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "A cold light is equipment which is placed on one side of the chest and if there is a pneumothorax within the chest, the light would spread all over the chest, which is called transillumination.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Immediately after the emergency chest drain was inserted, [Baby H] showed signs of improvement. She had good tidal volumes [that's the amount of air into her lungs] and her oxygen requirements were now 35%. [Baby H] was clinically much better after this procedure.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Once a chest drain is inserted, a further X-ray is required to confirm the drain is in the correct position and that the pneumothorax is resolved. A pneumothorax is air outside of the normal lung tissue.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: A pneumothorax can be small or large. A pneumothorax can be a possible side effect of CPAP.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Because [Baby H]'s mum was diabetic, [Baby H] was more likely to have a surfactant deficiency, surfactant being lubrication of the lungs, and as such was at greater risk of developing a pneumothorax. I recall apologising to [Baby H]'s parents when the first appropriate time was possible for not informing them of [Baby H]'s condition earlier. They then attended the unit at midday.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Registrar Harkness was with me when I apologised to the parents. Dr Gibbs also apologised to them later on in the day. The priority in such situations is the medical welfare of the baby. We always try to inform the parents as soon as possible, but not if it is going to compromise the health of the baby. If we felt that a baby was going to die then the parents would be informed straightaway. There was never any indication of this with [Baby H].
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I next updated the nursing notes at 18.49 hours, noting that [Baby H]'s chest drain had initially fluttered for 2 hours but this had now ceased. This indicated a large pneumothorax.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "[Baby H] remained on the ventilator and remained in oxygen between 38% to 50%. Her heart rate had remained stable throughout all procedures. Since the chest drain [Baby H] was pink and well perfused when previously she had been pale and mottled. [Baby H] did not pass much urine at 5 pm, developing oedemas around her feet, eyes and chin as a result. This was reported by myself to Registrar [Dr A]. [Baby H] was agitated when being handled, which could be for a variety of reasons, but can also indicate that she is in pain. As a result, I increased her morphine infusion as prescribed by doctors.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Registrar Harkness gave [Baby H] Curosurf, which is a surfactant and is administered through her endotracheal tube, to aid in gaseous exchange to improve oxygenation. At the end of my shift I handed over the care of [Baby H] to the night staff. I cannot recall who I handed over to that night.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "With reference to the early hours of 27 September 2015 I can confirm that I was on duty, working a night shift, but I am not noted on the nursing notes for [Baby H] that night and I didn't have anything to do with her care during that shift."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Next, my Lord, Dr Harkness' statement. In Dr Harkness' case there are some notes we'll refer to but once we get to the relevant point.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, certainly.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Witness statement of DR DAVID HARKNESS (read)
My Lord, this is a statement from Dr Harkness that's dated 20 April 2018. It reads as follows:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I have been asked to comment on [Baby H] and in particular her care on 24 September 2015. I can confirm that I was working a day shift on this day.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Having reviewed the clinical notes, I can recall [Baby H].
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "It has been handed over to me that she had some desaturations overnight. A recent chest X-ray was showing a left-sided pneumothorax and, at the time of my attendance for ward rounds, [Baby H]'s oxygen requirement had increased and she was starting to struggle, which suggested the pneumothorax was bigger than first thought. A cold light showed what had already been suspected.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "At this point the air from the pneumothorax needed to be drained quite quickly. I decided that a needle thoracocentesis was required to provide immediate release of air. This procedure involved the use of a butterfly needle attached to plastic tubing. The tubing is placed into sterile water to provide a seal whilst the needle is inserted underneath the middle of the clavicle, just below the second intercostal space.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: The sterile water should then bubble as the air is released. Completing this procedure showed an instant improvement to [Baby H]'s condition."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: The clavicle being the collarbone.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes, thank you:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Once the needle thoracocentesis is complete, you immediately insert a long-term chest drain line, which remains inside the patient, draining air from the pneumothorax. After this procedure, [Baby H] needed quite a lot on ventilatory settings and oxygen. An X-ray showed the chest drain was inserted correctly, inflating the lung. The plan was to do a blood gas 30 minutes later to ensure [Baby H]'s care was heading in the right direction and then start weaning her back down on the ventilation.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "All of my actions, reviews and plans were documented in the clinical notes and I had no other involvement with [Baby H] during this day."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Now, my Lord, having said that, if we go, please, to the EPE, and if we can go to tile 117, please. We can see a tile which deals with the morning of 25 September, the following day. If we go to the note itself, please, it's not covered in the statement, but I think we should look at it. It brings things up to date on 25 September. It's untimed, the note, but it begins "WR", which is the ward round, hence its position in the timeline.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: My Lord will see in a moment that there is a request for a blood test, which is timed at 10.44, so it's assumed to be round about 10 am. That's why it appears where it does in the sequence of events.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: It sets out the gestation period and present age of [Baby H]. The problems set out are a left tension pneumothorax, two chest drains and five needle thoracocentesis, RDS and, I presume, sepsis. I'm not going to go through the whole of the entry in any great detail unless I'm asked to do so, simply to point out, bearing in mind the issues, V is ventilation, and that shows a pressure of 20/5. And on the right-hand side, the oxygen concentration, which has been referred to by Dr Harkness and indeed other witnesses already this morning, is now at 28%.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: If we look, please, at the chest drain section, if we can scroll up a little bit, please. It may be relevant with subsequent doctors. The chest drains are described as:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Fifth space not swinging and serous fluid from drain. Seventh space swinging and bubbly."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think it was Dr Harkness himself who explained that the next diagram is showing that the chest was clear with good air entry and good chest movement.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: If we can scroll down again, please. We can just deal with the bottom of this page first. I know my learned friend would like me to deal with some matters on the next page. There's a reference there to TPN by way of nutrition, passing urine, bowels open. The diagram of the bowel -- sorry, the stomach was soft, no masses, bowel sounds plus. And on the right, bearing in mind the concern about blood sugars, we've got a BM of 4.5.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: If we can go to the next page, please, Mr Murphy.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: I understand CNS refers to central nervous system and next to that particular entry:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Splints diaphragm and desats on all handling. No abnormal movements."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Before we leave that, we can see that the blood pressure in the -- mean blood pressure is 42 to 49.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Scroll down again, please.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Would it be possible for -- we're going to have a medical expert --
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Mm.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Um... It's not what I'd hope to see as such, but I wouldn't -- serous wouldn't mean infection to me. I'd expect it to be more sort of -- less clear -- I'd have said purulent or a bit pussy, you'd see an infection there.

blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: In this context?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, yes.

blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.

blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.

blocks.text: Next entry:
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: You just need to go down on the next --
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Forgive me, I'm looking at a piece of paper. Mr Murphy, if we could scroll down to J12539, please.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Sorry, Dr Ventress, I got ahead of the screen there.

blocks.text: Apologies:
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So could you, with the benefit or the assistance of your notes, Dr Ventress, tell us what happened at 01.25?

blocks.text: So [Baby H] again desaturated and this time her sats went down into the 30s. She had an increasingly mottled appearance at that time. I've written she had poor chest movement but the capnograph was still changing colour. And I called the consultant to attend at that time. I'd have asked one of the nurses to call the consultant.

blocks.text: For what particular purpose?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: To come in and assist.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Thank you. What was your working theory at this point?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So the next thing I've written was a question mark, query the tension pneumothorax had re-accumulated, so that was my thought of what was going on. So I performed an emergency needle thoracocentesis at 01.30.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Thank you. We know that previously a chest drain had been fitted.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Your cold light test a little earlier was indicative of a potential recurrence of the problem to the left --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And that was the basis of your --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: -- your theory, working theory here, and the reason why you intervened in the way you did?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: To drain the air out on an emergency, immediate basis?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.

blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.

blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes. So I'd had the appropriate training and things, but that's the first time that I'd had to actually do it on a baby, yes.

blocks.text: So a memorable event.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And so do you in the next entry give the detail of that procedure --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: -- as undertaken by you at 01.30? And then the consequence, the results from it, that you aspirated 70 millilitres of air?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And how did that go?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So 70ml of air is quite a lot for a baby that size. And things improved after that. Her sats improved to around 90%, although she was still requiring 100% additional oxygen.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: So from that improved data, did that tend to confirm that your working theory that had caused you to act on an emergency basis was right?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And you'd solved that immediate problem --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: -- there and then?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: The next entry evidences that a chest X-ray was performed. I should say in terms of our carousel, the emergency procedure is noted at tile 46 and this X-ray is noted at tile 48.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So an X-ray was performed. You, it would seem, considered the radiograph.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. I would have seen it, yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And what did it tell you?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: It says it still showed a large left-sided tension pneumothorax but mainly in the lower chest area.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Thank you. So again, did that tend to confirm the underlying problem that you'd feared --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: It confirmed the diagnosis of a tension pneumothorax, but also showed that there were still a good amount of air remaining, despite the procedure.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: So the 70ml was progress, but the problem not yet solved?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Your next entry is timed at 01.45, which is behind our tile 49. What did you observe at 01.45?

blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Thank you. Is this right that -- so the butterfly needle was the equipment that you used for this emergency procedure?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: You see it go into the water and cause the water to bubble? That's what you want to see?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: So it was under the water but the bubbling had ceased?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: So that draining process had --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Had stopped at that point, yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And because of what you'd seen on the X-ray, was it right that you deemed it appropriate to effectively repeat it but lower down --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: -- in the chest --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: -- to get at that air that was evident on --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: -- the X-ray? And it worked, it would seem.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, we got a further 60ml of air, yes. And I've written her sats then recovered.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Right. So second phase problem solving?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And second phase progress?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Your note told us that you'd called for a consultant and this part of your note tells us that the consultant, Dr Jayaram, arrived at 01.50?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Which event is on our carousel at tile 50.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Talk us through your note, if you would, please, at this point, 01.50 onwards.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So increased PIP, so increased the pressure that the ventilator was giving, to 28/5 -- sorry, on the Neopuff.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: It's a similar setting to the ventilator but using the Neopuff. So it gave her more pressure. She was still being bagged on the Neopuff at this point. I repeated the chest X-ray, which showed still some tension pneumothorax, although a slight improvement from the previous one. Then we did a lateral shoot-through Xray. Usually X-rays are done front to back, but you can do them side to side to look at it from that angle.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: So that showed us that the pocket of air outside the lungs was very anterior, so right under the surface at the top.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Right. If anyone's interested, that X-ray is recorded at tile 55 on our carousel.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So consequently, was a third needle aspiration tried?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: But without, this time, any consequent aspiration of air?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Moving forward in time, looking at your next entry at 02.40, which is behind tile 57, tell the jury, please, what this note informs us of.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So I've written that the ET tube was removed as [Baby H]'s sats had reduced to 80% in 100% oxygen and the capnograph had stopped changing colour. So we'd assumed that the ET tube was blocked or dislodged at that point if the capnograph is not changing colour at all.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Right.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So therefore I removed the tube. And when the tube was removed, I've written it appeared completely blocked with a mucus plug.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Right. So your assumption was correct. So this is an additional problem?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: So we've had the problem with the tension pneumothorax, which you've tried to address with varying degrees of success in the preceding hour or so. But then this is an additional problem, mucus blocking the ET tube?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: So did you then seek to address that problem?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. We took the tube out and then re-intubated her a couple of minutes later, by the SHO, Dr Varghese again, and was successful on the first attempt. And it looked straightforward from the notes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: So she was re-intubated and did that work?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I think so. I need to go down on the notes again.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Oh sorry. Apologies.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, so the chest movement was much improved and her sats improved and the amount of oxygen she was needing lessened. We put her back on the ventilator successfully that time.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Thank you. If anybody cares to make a note, the event at 02.40 is behind tile 57. The event at 02.45 is behind tile 58.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Then we have an entry noted at 03.00 and I think Mr Murphy very kindly has offered to put the next page up behind this and I invite him to do so. So we'll give Dr Ventress the opportunity to remind herself of the full note before we ask her about it. If we look at the bottom of J12539, please, Mr Murphy, so Dr Ventress can read the full flow of the sentence. And then overleaf.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: (Pause)
So at 03.00 hours, which is an event behind tile 61 on our carousel, what happened at about 03.00 hours?
So [Baby H] had another desaturation episode down to 26% oxygen, I've documented, this time.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Sorry, can I just go back to the previous page, the last sentence?
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So we did another needle aspiration, this time in the 7th intercostal space, so even lower than before, which was successful.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Overleaf, thank you, Mr Murphy.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: And 85ml of air were aspirated and her sats improved.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: So that was a successful procedure.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Thank you. So the earlier chest X-ray had shown an accumulation of air in the lower part of the chest.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: You'd had one attempt to get at that without the desired result. So you went even lower?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And this time you hit the spot?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Thank you. Then the final entry here informs us that a further chest X-ray was taken. And for the note, that is recorded behind tile 66 at a time of 03.05 hours. What did that inform you of, Dr Ventress?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So the ET tube position I've written was okay, satisfactory, and the left lung was much better inflated now compared with previous X-rays.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Thank you. A plan was drawn up?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. A plan to insert a further chest drain. She already had one, I think, at this point, and we planned to insert another one. But I've written, "No Seldinger drains available", which are the type I'd been trained on how to put in, so a different type of drain was inserted by the consultant.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Thank you. So taking a step back and considering all those events that you noted up at 03.30, but that took place between 01.14 and a little after 3 am, is this a fair summary, that there was a tension pneumothorax to the left --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: -- as evidenced by a cold light and an X-ray?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And incrementally, you addressed that problem?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And managed to aspirate all the air?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: A good amount, yes. Have you had explained the difference between a pneumothorax and a tension pneumothorax before?
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Please do.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Just because that is, I think, an important point in this. So any pneumothorax is air around the lung between the lung and the chest wall. In a tension pneumothorax there's almost a valve that's -- it could be sort of the wound is like this (indicating), so it's letting air out of the lung but it's not letting any air back into the lung, so more and more air just fills this space and compresses the lung, can compress the heart and the blood vessels as well, whereas in just a straightforward pneumothorax you can get air in and out of the lung from that space.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: A tension pneumothorax is a true emergency whereas just air around the lung itself isn't necessarily.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And in this context, does tension refer to pressure?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. It's pressure in that space between the lung and the chest wall.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And we'll see in some notes some clinicians noting whether or not the heart has moved?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Is that because that's a real worry?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So in a tension, the heart and the midline moves over to the opposite side on the X-ray. That would explain why she was mottled and her capillary refill time was prolonged earlier on in the episode.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: So the pressure, is this right, can compromise the effective function of not just the lung but also the heart?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: And the main blood vessels it can compress a little, yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Thank you. And that was one of the problems that manifested in these hours in the early hours of the 25th?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: But you addressed them?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And at or during that period of time there was also the mucus-blocked ET tube?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Which was also addressed by removal and re-intubation?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: So it was a rocky night for [Baby H]?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: But were the causes for those problems identified?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. So a tension pneumothorax is something that does happen. We never can find the exact cause for it, but a premature baby needing CPAP or respiratory support, a pneumothorax and a tension pneumothorax is a known complication of that. So yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And the pressing problems were successfully addressed?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: My Lord, we're now going to move on to a different shift where there were significant events.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: If we are to have a break this morning, this might be a convenient time.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Certainly, we will have a break now.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: A ten-minute break then, please, members of the jury.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Ten minutes, thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Doctor, a ten-minute break and then continuing.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes, that's fine.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: (A short break)
I wonder if I could ask Mr Murphy to put tile 210 up. Thank you. It informs us all that we've now moved forward in time to 23.50 hours on Friday, 25 September.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: We're about to look at some of your notes, which inform us that you were working nights again.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: The 25th into the 26th; is that right?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, that's right.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: At 23.50, so approaching midnight on 25 September, you made the note that is in part on screen at the moment.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Is this a note that you've familiarised yourself with recently?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, it is.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Thank you. It begins by informing the reader that [Baby H] had had several episodes of desaturation in the previous 2 hours. The remainder of this note, which sets out those two -those episodes, I should say, were they episodes that you observed and witnessed or did you receive a report of the episodes or can't you remember?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I can't tell from those notes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Okay. So the first of the recorded episodes, the note tells us, was:
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: "After gas taken (good gas) became agitated."
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Could you explain that to us?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. So the first desaturation in this cluster, I would assume that was reported to me, but I can't be sure. It was reported to happen after she had blood gas taken, so would have had a heel prick blood test done. And then "good gas" indicates a satisfactory blood gas result at that point.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Right. So the baby became agitated after a heel prick test was undertaken?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And is that an uncommon response?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No, it's not uncommon.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: It was noted that yellow serous fluid was coming from the drain, quantity 8ml. Does the colour inform you of anything in particular?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No. Yellow serous fluid doesn't sound anything worrying.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Thank you. And eventually, the baby improved with bagging, with Neopuffing?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Another of the episodes you note was associated with poor chest movement, a bradycardia, and in consequence, is this right, the ET tube was suctioned and a thick mucus substance was produced through that active suctioning?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And your note suggests that thereafter the chest movement improved and her saturation levels increased?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: The next entry:
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: "10ml of air aspirated from pigtail drain."
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Could you just expand upon that a little for us?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So I'd attempted to aspirate air from one of the chest drains that [Baby H] had in because sometimes the chest drain could become blocked with fluid and there was air collecting again. So I aspirated 10ml, so there was a little bit of air but not as much as the previous night when it was 70/80ml.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Thank you. You performed another cold light test and on this occasion that produced a negative result?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: This note began by informing us there were several episodes, so you pick up upon that series of events by saying:
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: "Further episodes. No change in heart rate.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Recovered with bagging on higher pressure."
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: And the ventilation was increased.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: It speaks for itself. The next entry. What does that inform us of?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So between these episodes of desaturation, [Baby H] was only requiring 30% oxygen to maintain normal saturation levels.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Thank you. A repeat chest X-ray was performed?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: For the purpose, does it flow from your note, of seeking to establish whether there was still a tension pneumothorax evident?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Did you consider that chest X-ray?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, I will have done. I think the stickers are somewhere else in the note.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Thank you. The final note here, please, at 23.50.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So I've put, based on the chest X-ray, there was a significant pneumo mediastinum. That was air in the central part of the chest surrounding the main vessels in the oesophagus and windpipe and things. That can happen when there's air leak in other places as well but you can't put a needle or a drain into that to solve it.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Right.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So that just disappears on its own eventually. Then the second chest drain advanced back in to 4 centimetres as it was almost out. I have written that was done prior to the chest X-ray. So yes, it speaks for itself.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Right. Could you help us understand it? Does that indicate that the second chest drain was in a sub-optimal position?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. So it had almost fallen out of [Baby H].
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And would that prevent or at least reduce its function?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: So you fixed that problem --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: -- by replacing it? Thank you.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: For the note, that entry at 23.50 that Dr Ventress has just helped us understand is behind tile 210.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: The next note is behind tile 216. I think possibly a slip of the pen here, Dr Ventress, but it's timed at 01.00 --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: -- because you have said below therefore the date must be the 26th rather than the 25th.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: It happens surprisingly often on night shifts!
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Yes. What is it that you noted at 1 in the morning on the 26th?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So her oxygen requirements had gradually increased up to 70%, but I've written there's been no further profound desaturation since around midnight. Then she had a poor blood gas, which shows a low pH and a high carbon dioxide level. And by the time I'd written that, she was now in 100% oxygen.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Right. So the degree of respiratory support provided was being significantly increased; is that right?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: The amount of oxygen, additional oxygen, she was requiring had gone up, yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Thank you. What, if any, effect did that have?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So I then increased the ventilation support and increased the rate of the ventilator and the pressure she was getting. But then her blood pressure started to drop, so the combination of needing more oxygen, more respiratory support and a drop in blood pressure made me think, had she got another pneumothorax like the previous night.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: So did you undertake a test?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. We did the cold light test again, which showed it was slightly brighter in the left but not transilluminating the whole side of the chest. So I called the consultant that night, Dr Gibbs, for advice, and he said he'd come and review the patient.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Right. What is it about that -- what was it, I should say -- about that combination of data and the results of the cold light test that caused you to deem it necessary to call the consultant?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I think if the cold light had given me a clear result that she had another tension pneumothorax then it would have been clear what treatment she needed, but because it hadn't given that clear result and she was clearly unwell, needing lots of oxygen, higher support and her blood pressure was dropping then I felt at that stage I needed additional advice at least on how to progress from then.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Thank you. We know that Dr Gibbs did attend. Dr Gibbs has made a note. Would you have been with Dr Gibbs when he came and examined [Baby H]?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: In that case --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I may not have been with him for the whole time he was there if it was hours, if I'd got called back to the paediatric ward, but I would have been there for the initial -- when he arrived, yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: In that case could we go to tile 228, Mr Murphy? It is Dr Gibbs' notes, which in the clinical notes follows immediately after your entry that we've just considered.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Can you recall, were you part of this examination, did you interact with Dr Gibbs, did you act upon any of his conclusions or were you elsewhere or can you not remember?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I can't remember exactly and these couple of notes do muddle up in your memory.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Right.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: But yes, as I said, I'd have been there when he arrived and given him a handover of what had happened during the night, but from that he's documented that he put another chest drain in, so at that stage I may have been elsewhere.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Right. We'll defer to Dr Gibbs then.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: At least we've established in the timeline that a further chest drain was fitted --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: -- at this point or thereabouts, 02.15. Your next entry in the notes follows on immediately from Dr Gibbs' entry. It's behind tile 243, which is, as we'll see now, a note made at 04.00 hours.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: But a retrospective note, which begins by informing the reader that you responded to a crash call at 03.24 hours; is that right?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, that's right.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: So upon receiving that signal, did you attend and go straight to nursery 1 --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: -- where we know [Baby H] was housed at this point of time?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: She, you were informed, am I right, had had a further desaturation which required Neopuffing?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: That her sats, as recalled, had fallen into the 60s?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Is that a level of real concern, 60s?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Then help us, please, with the remainder of this note.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So her sats had fallen to the 60s?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Then the heart rate had dropped to less than 100, so at that point the nurses put out a crash call. So I wasn't there for that part. I have written later on "on my arrival", so everything before that was before I arrived.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Thank you. Were you informed that, prior to this development, the baby was not being handled at all?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And no trigger identified?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Does that in a way echo the note we looked at earlier where there was a certain adverse reaction to the heel pricking?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. Desaturations aren't that uncommon in babies on a ventilator, but often there will be something, they've had suction, they've had a blood test, they've had their nappy changed, lots of things that have happened to them that might trigger it off.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: So one of the things you do, am I right, you look for a stimulus to see whether there's a cause and effect?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: The next entry, please, towards the bottom of this page.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: "No trigger identified. Not fitting."
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: So one thing that I would think about with regular desaturations where no cause is identified is could the baby be having a seizure, but there's no sign of that there.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Right.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Then I have written she just finished a 10ml per kg saline bolus -- does that say 30 minutes before? So I think that had been prescribed by Dr Gibbs probably, but she just finished that 30 minutes before.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Is there any particular reason why you've included that in this note?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Um... (Pause). I think it's just getting the timings involved. It's not particularly related to what happened at that time, but just to -- you know, I was aware she'd just had a fluid bolus, so there were concerns before that about her perfusion, I'd imagine, if she was given a fluid bolus.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Thank you. We will defer to Dr Gibbs on that in due course. But if we continue with your note, which goes on to another page, but Mr Murphy's very helpfully attached it to the bottom of this, so we could scroll, please.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: This is a continuation of the same note that you've just assisted us with; is that right?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And talk us through this down to the heart rate reading, please.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. On my arrival to the neonatal unit, she was being bagged via her breathing tube. They were achieving good chest movement and the capnograph colour change was positive, so the tube was in a good position and effectively moving air in and out of the lungs.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Right. So if there was a problem it wasn't the --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: It wasn't that the tube was blocked.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: No. The chest movement and capnograph indicator informed you of that?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Yet, is it fair for me to add that word, her sats were still at 60% and the heart rate was dropping --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: -- yet further from 70 to 50?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, that's fair.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: That's a very serious problem; is that right?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Your next entry times your intervention at 03.26. For the purpose of the note this is on our carousel behind tile 244, but we'll just stay with this note.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Please explain the events that you've recorded as of 03.26.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So chest compressions, CPR, were started at 03.26, as her heart rate was less than 60, and Dr Gibbs was called back in. So he'd left at some time but I'm not sure when. blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: If we could break that down, please, Dr Ventress. We all, I'm sure, understand the CPR being commenced. In terms of the degree of that intervention, of that response to the data, does that indicate that this was a very, very real emergency?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. She was having full resuscitation, yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Because of what you'd observed the previous night, you understandably repeated a cold light test. What was the degree of the results of that cold light test?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I have just written that the left was brighter than the right. I can't remember more than that.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Very well. You repeated the emergency procedure that you'd done for the very first time on an earlier shift.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: And the results on this occasion were the aspiration of 2ml of air and 2ml of fluid. Again, in terms of degree, was that a very significant level of aspirate?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No. There was 8ml of air and 2ml of fluid, but no, not significant enough to have caused the issues -- the state that [Baby H] was in at the time.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: You then break down, on a minute-by-minute basis, the interventions which were part of the emergency response; is that right?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: At 03.30 -- and if anyone's interested the 03.30 event is recorded behind tiles 245 and 246 -- you gave the child adrenaline --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: -- 0.25ml. Again, Dr Ventress, was that something you'd done many times?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. This is standard advanced life support at this stage. So she's -- we treat a heart rate of less than 60 in a neonate of a cardiac arrest so this is basically a cardiac arrest treatment plan. She does have a heart rate, she's not got a zero heart rate, but less than 60 we treat as if zero.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: So you go to the cardiac arrest protocol --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: -- effectively?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And is that -- we'll go through them and is that what we will see --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: -- recorded between 03.30 and 03.46?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: It is, yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Thank you. So adrenaline introduced at 03.30. A note made at -- sorry, referring to events of 03.32, which are behind our tile 247. Can you expand upon that note, please, the 3.32 note?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So I've written the heart rate was reading 92 on the monitor and her sats were reading 70%, but as soon as the chest compressions were stopped the heart rate decreased again. So it would have been one of the nurses probably providing chest compressions and you do sometimes -- if they are providing good quality chest compressions you do get a heart rate and sats pick
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: up from them because they are moving blood successfully round the body.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: So the chest compressions had a positive effect whilst they were being applied?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: However, once stopped, did things revert?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, the heart rate dropped again, yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: So the underlying problem, whatever it may have been, had not been solved?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Hence at 03.35, and this is behind tile 248, a further dose of adrenaline was given?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Not in your notes, but Dr Gibbs' notes below will tell us that he arrived at 03.36, in between your two entries, and that event is recorded behind our tile 250.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So Dr Gibbs arrived but he supplies us with the time of 03.36.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Next, at 03.39, this is our tile 251, further adrenaline and then, 03.45, our tile 253, what was given then and why?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So atropine was given, which is medication to prevent bradycardia. It's part of, again, the cardiac -- it's a... It's not a compulsory part, but it is part of the cardiac arrest algorithm, yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: So a further and later stage?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And can we draw from the fact that it was given that it was deemed necessary to move to that further and later stage of this --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: -- algorithm, this protocol; yes?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And then by 03.46, and this is our tile 255, what had happened and what took place?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: The chest compressions were stopped as the heart rate had improved to 120 and then to 160, and the heart rate stayed high and her colour started improving.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: So the emergency response --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Had worked, yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: -- was, thankfully, successful?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Thank you. Dr Gibbs will give evidence in due course and will expand upon the note that he made.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Could we then move on, please. Just confirm, Dr Ventress, was that the last time you had direct involvement with [Baby H] as best you can recall?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, as far as I've seen.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Perhaps you would have been there whilst Dr Gibbs responded to your request for his attendance, but does it follow that he effectively would have taken --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Taken the lead, yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: -- taken the lead in the half an hour or so immediately after the event that you've just described to us?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Dr Ventress, as part of the timeline of these events that we've looked at, the jury have seen yesterday a number of text messages or other social media communications involving some members of staff at the hospital, including yourself.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: I'm not going to go through them all, but can I just take you to a couple and ask you what you recall and to explain your communications rather than somebody else's.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Before I do so, to give it some context, you were clearly directly involved in the events that we've considered, in
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: particular the one we've just considered a moment ago that called for CPR.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Did you subsequently have reported to you that there had been a further significant event involving [Baby H] whilst you were absent, presumably having some time off having done a series of nights? Do you remember?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I can't remember. Probably.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: If we could just look at tile 511, please. Just to get the time and date. We've just been looking at, haven't we, events that took place in the early hours of 26 September? blocks.text: "[Baby H] had resus again but not as long-lasting as it was for us. She went to Arrowe."

blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No, that was the first night, the 24th, I think it was, yes.

blocks.text: But of course the events at 03.30 or thereabouts on the 26th that we've just focused on, that was --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, that was resus.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: That was resus, yes. The next tile, please, to see -- do you recognise this as your response to the message we've just looked at?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Cross-examination by MR MYERS
Do you agree, Dr Ventress, that there are numerous reasons why a baby on a ventilator with chest drains may desaturate?
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And do you agree that a desaturation in those circumstances is not uncommon?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: You've been asked about a comment about "no trigger identified" that was in your notes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Do you recall that? Sometimes it's possible to see an action or a process that's taken place that leads to a direct negative consequence in a baby, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And if you can do that, and you gave examples like suction, blood test or a nappy change, if you can do that then you can draw the link and say that must be what's caused it or played a part.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: In fact, if we look at the days leading up to the event at about 03.20 on 26 September there's a good deal more than just suction, a nappy change and a blood test that had happened, isn't there?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: I'm going to summarise, we may look at some of the detail, but over those days there had been multiple desaturations of this little girl, hadn't there?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And indeed, in the hours leading up to the event we're looking at, there had been a series of desaturations, hadn't there?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And some of those desaturations had been what's described as profound?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, I'd agree.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: She had been suffering certainly at points, and maybe for prolonged periods of time, from a tension pneumothorax, hadn't she?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And that can constitute a medical emergency, can't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, definitely.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And that is likely to put a strain on the little body of a neonate like this, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: She had also over the period leading up to this event had three chest drains inserted, hadn't she?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, that's right.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: We've heard that handling can play a part in putting a baby under distress so that they might desaturate; that's right, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, handling.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And would you agree, one chest drain is quite an event for a baby to undergo; that's right, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Three of them is a lot of pressure on that baby, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And the third of those chest drains was put in at about 2.15 on the morning we're looking at, wasn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, if that's what the note say, yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: So a little more than an hour before this event?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And in addition to chest drains, she'd also had what are called butterfly needles inserted --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: -- on multiple occasions, hadn't she?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And even at 1 o'clock in the morning before this event, your opinion was that she was clearly unwell at that point, wasn't she?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, she's been clearly unwell throughout this, yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: All right. And even at 01.00 she needed lots of oxygen, didn't she?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: That's in the note, that's what you said, sorry. And her blood pressure was dropping at that point?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: When you come to look at the totality of what her body had gone through over a period of 3 days, that was a significant amount of strain on a baby, wasn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, I agree.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: So it's right that we can't identify something like a nappy change or suction or a heel prick or something like that shortly before the collapse?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Is this the arrest that we're talking about?
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's not the bit that I said no trigger identified for, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: What bit did that apply to?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That was earlier on in the notes, wasn't it?
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: We can see if you want to check. It's at tile 228.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Could we look there, please? We'll just be clear.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Page 12548.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Oh yeah. Does that carry on into the arrest? Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: That's it. So that is what we're talking about, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes. Thank you for clarifying.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: So what I said was correct, wasn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: Thank you. So although we have no trigger identified at the note we understand why you put that there.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: The reality is, she had been through an awful lot of medical activity, hadn't she?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: VENTRESS

blocks.text: And it is quite conceivable that a baby under that much intervention, having gone through what she had gone through, could suffer quite a significant collapse?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.

blocks.text: So cumulatively, over 3 days, it could be said that did contribute to what happened?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

NURSE D: So when I took over the care of [Baby H], she was on a ventilator on a mode of SIMV, which is simultaneous mandatory ventilation. She was on pressures of 24/4 with a rate of 50. Over the morning, following each gas, we were able to wean down the pressures and recheck her blood gases an hour after reducing the pressures.

Also she was reviewed -- the gases were reviewed by the doctors on the ward round and once again the tidal volumes were slightly raised so her pressure was reduced again and rechecked an hour after that. So the pressures were reduced as per [Baby H]'s requirements throughout the morning.
If we could go over that very briefly and break it down.

blocks.text: There were a series of blood gas tests undertaken; correct?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: NURSE D: Yes.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: And the results considered?

blocks.text: NURSE D: Yes, reviewed by the doctors.

blocks.text: NURSE D: Yes, progress. The pressures were reduced following each gas.

blocks.text: Thank you. At 12.30 there was -- we're about four or five lines down to this note -- there was an event or some reaction from [Baby H] that was of note; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: NURSE D: Yes. The mode of ventilation had been changed to CMV, which is -- the SIMV allows the baby to put in some breaths themselves as well as what the ventilator is set for, whereas CMV will have the set rate of, in [Baby H]'s case, 50 breaths per minute. So she'd been put on that, on a previous gas, but had then begun to breathe against the ventilator as well so the doctors reviewed that and changed her back to the SIMV to allow her to put more breaths in independently as well. That was at 12.30.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: And also, they increased the dose of morphine to help settle her a little bit more as well on the ventilator.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Right. So was that given to make her more compliant --

blocks.text: NURSE D: To help settle her a little bit more so she wasn't as actively breathing against the ventilator.

If there are any secretions beginning to build up then it can be slightly creaky or we can hear it louder through auscultation on to the chest wall with the stethoscope. So we would check that to ensure that the airway was patent really, the tube was -- the breaths were being delivered clearly.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Thank you. Could we please, Mr Murphy, scroll down to the bottom paragraph on this side of the page, in the heading of which we can see an addendum at 13.55. It's now a note made at 13.55, but reference to events that include something at 08.25.

blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: movement through that drain. But the other chest drain was moving intermittently throughout the shift.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: To assist those of us who aren't experienced in this field, where it says "the chest drain was swinging", does that actually literally mean it was swinging?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: NURSE D: The two drains -- she had two different chest drains in place. So a flutter valve is a small plastic tube with like a gauze layer in and that will move as the air is coming out. blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: All right. So swinging is a reference to the movement of fluid rather than the movement of --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: NURSE D: Yes.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: -- the drain?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: NURSE D: Movement of the fluid through the chest drain line.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Thank you.

blocks.text: So the tube was removed?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: NURSE D: Yes.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Was it blocked?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: NURSE D: I don't remember. I have not documented whether it was blocked or not.

blocks.text: So it having been removed, according to your note, the doctors arrived, [Baby H] was being bagged with Neopuff, and the next entry, spontaneously breathing.

blocks.text: So does it follow from that that there was desaturation, lack of respiration, until the ET tube was removed?

blocks.text: NURSE D: Yes, there was no chest movement and I couldn't hear any air entry either via the ET tube, so I felt the ET tube was either blocked with secretions or was dislodged.

blocks.text: But once I removed it I was able to give her some mandatory breaths and expand her lungs and increase her oxygen saturations.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: And upon the removal of the ET tube and those interventions you've just described, things improved?

blocks.text: NURSE D: Yes.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER
